person_note: The controlling narration is third person. The long Goodreads opening scene is diagnostic and matches the authorized excerpt, which moves among Grace, Judith, and Wayne while narrating their perceptions and thoughts externally. The historical horse passage likewise presents a nonparticipating authorial voice; its generic you does not create second-person narration. Shorter third-person quotations were conservatively left unmarked, and all first-person language occurs in dialogue or gnomic material. The whole-book point-of-view description explicitly corroborates third-person omniscience, while Evans's account of using several main-character viewpoints is consistent with shifting third-person focalization rather than alternating grammatical persons. No credible contrary person structure was found.
